correctness.rationale: I reconstructed exact counting from the coefficients D_k(q) of the signed-sum Laurent product with factor sum_{d=-3}^3 binom(6,3+d) X^(d*3^j) at digit j. Selecting the lowest digit gives D_(k+1)(q)=sum_{d=q mod 3} binom(6,3+d) D_k((q-d)/3). Symmetry leaves the closed pair (D_k(0),D_k(1)), with matrix rows (20,2) and (15,6), starting at (1,0). Its trace and determinant are 26 and 90; solving at k=0,1 gives the stated numerator and root coefficients. An independently written coefficient convolution also matched the recurrence at k=0 through 9 (E_9=1030671951680). The set of sums at k+1 is four translates of the previous interval separated by 3^k; the previous upper endpoint is at least 3^k-1, including k=0. Hence the intervals cover the claimed support, and the 8^k ordered triples give the benchmark 64^k/S_k. The leading coefficient, growth base greater than one, and Fourier identity follow from the root solution and ordinary integer-frequency orthogonality. The supporting script was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The finite independent convolution is corroboration only. The theorem counts ordinary integer equality, not equality modulo 3^k.
